html:
A Polish astronomer and churchman who put the Sun, not the Earth, at the centre of the planets. His book On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres came out in 1543, the year he died.

He was born in Toruń, in the Kingdom of Poland, studied at Kraków and then in Italy at Bologna and Padua, and spent most of his life as a canon of the cathedral at Frombork, also working as a doctor and writing on money.

Since Ptolemy in the 100s CE, astronomers had put a still Earth at the centre, with the planets moving on circles upon circles. Copernicus argued that a moving Earth, turning daily on its axis and circling the Sun yearly, explained the planets' odd backward loops more simply. The idea was not wholly new: the Greek Aristarchus had suggested it. His model still used perfect circles and was not more accurate at first.

Few were convinced for decades. Then Kepler, Galileo and finally Newton built on it, and the Copernican revolution came to stand for any great change of viewpoint.
sum: A Polish astronomer and churchman who put the Sun, not the Earth, at the centre of the planets. His book On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres came out in 1543, the year he died.
